Pexi: Terms, Privacy and Data

Effective 2026-11-25. This covers version 1.0 of the Pexi app for iPhone and Android and the server it talks to.

Everything about using Pexi, in one place: the Terms of Use, the Privacy Policy, what Pexi records, where its prices come from and how Pexi Plus works.

Tapping Accept and continue, or using Pexi, means you agree to all of it. If you do not agree, do not use Pexi.

Who we are and what Pexi is

Pexi is published by Jamin Xu, an individual developer. Pexi lets you scan a barcode or type a product name and shows whether the price of the item is great, good, reasonable or bad compared with prices Pexi holds or estimates.

Jamin Xu is the person in charge of the protection of personal information for Pexi, including for the purposes of Quebec's privacy law. Questions, access requests and deletion requests go to him at usepexiapp@gmail.com.

The short version

  • Pexi has no account, no sign-in, and does not ask for your name, email address, phone number or payment details.
  • Your phone makes a random identifier for itself the first time you open Pexi. Pexi's server uses it to recognise the same phone on later requests. It is not your name, but everything Pexi records is tied to it.
  • Pexi records what you scan or type, what it answered, and how you use the app, and uses it to make its answers better.
  • When your phone lets Pexi use location, Pexi sends only a rough area about one kilometre wide, never your exact position.
  • This version of Pexi does not upload photos or camera images.
  • When Pexi has no price for a product, the product's name, brand, size, category and country go to Anthropic's Claude AI to estimate a typical price. This is part of how Pexi answers.
  • Pexi deletes what it records on a stated schedule. See "How long Pexi keeps it" below.
  • If you subscribe to Pexi Plus, Apple (on iPhone) or Google Play (on Android) processes the payment and RevenueCat, a subscription service, records the purchase against the same random identifier. Pexi never sees your card, Apple ID or Google account details.
  • Pexi does not show ads, does not use advertising or analytics companies (RevenueCat is used only to manage subscriptions), and does not track you across other companies' apps or websites.

Who can use Pexi

Pexi is for people of all ages. If you are under the age of majority where you live, use Pexi with the permission of a parent or guardian, who accepts this document on your behalf. A purchase of Pexi Plus is made through the Apple ID or Google account on the device, under Apple's or Google's own rules for family members and purchases.

Pexi asks no one for a name, email address, birth date or account, and it collects the same information described here from every user, whatever their age. A parent or guardian who wants a child's information deleted can email usepexiapp@gmail.com, and the records tied to that device will be deleted. If you are under 14, please ask a parent or guardian before you allow location or share a price you typed.

Prices and estimates are information only

Everything Pexi shows about a price is informational. A verdict, a price range or a comparison is Pexi's estimate, and is labelled that way. Pexi does not guarantee that any price, range, verdict, product name or store detail is accurate, complete or current. Prices change, stores differ by location and date, and Pexi does not check every store. Always rely on the price displayed by the store, and on your receipt, when you decide whether to buy. Pexi is a decision aid, not advice, and nothing it shows is an offer, a quote or a promise that a store will honour a price.

AI price estimates

When Pexi has no price of its own for a product, it shows a typical price range generated by Anthropic's Claude AI model, labelled as estimated by AI. AI-generated content can be wrong, out of date, or based on a guess about what a product is. Treat all AI-generated content as unverified.

To make the estimate, Pexi's server sends Anthropic the product's name, brand, size, category and country. If you typed the name and Pexi did not recognise it, your typed words are the name it receives. Anthropic does not receive images, your device identifier or your location. Pexi saves the estimate. Sending these product details to Claude is part of using Pexi.

What Pexi records

A random device identifier. Your phone generates it and keeps it on the phone, in the phone's secure storage (the Keychain on iPhone, Android's encrypted storage on Android) and in the app's own storage, together with a second random secret that proves later requests come from the same phone. Both are sent to Pexi's server with the requests the app makes. On iPhone the Keychain can outlast the app, so reinstalling Pexi on the same phone keeps the same identifier and your scan count. On Android, deleting the app normally removes the identifier, so a reinstall usually starts with a new one.

What you scan or type. When you scan a barcode, Pexi sends the barcode digits. When you type a product name, Pexi sends the text you typed. While the camera is open, Pexi's app reads text that is visible in the camera view using text recognition that runs on your phone, and sends the recognised lines of text (not the image) to Pexi's server to find matching products. These are stored with the answer Pexi gave, whether Pexi answered or could not, any correction you made, and the time.

Prices, stores and ratings you enter. If you type the price you saw on a shelf, choose a store, tell Pexi a verdict was wrong, or rate a verdict, that is stored with the scan. When you type a price or pick a product, Pexi also stores a scrambled one-way code of your network (never your IP address) to keep fake prices out, and removes it together with your device identifier.

How you use the app. Pexi records when the app is opened, which screens you visit, buttons you tap, errors the app hits, and text you send, such as a search. Text you delete or leave unsent is not recorded; Pexi records only that a search was left unfinished.

Your acceptance. Pexi records that you accepted this document, which version, and when.

Technical details of each request. The app version, the platform, how long an answer took, and your language and market setting. Pexi's server also logs, for every request, the time, the web address requested, the response status, your IP address, the country the request came from, and your phone's user agent text.

Purchase history, only if you subscribe. Pexi Plus is sold through Apple's in-app purchase system on iPhone and Google Play Billing on Android. The purchase is made with Apple or Google, and RevenueCat records which plan you bought, when it renews and whether it is active, under your random device identifier as the app user identifier. The app checks your subscription with RevenueCat each time it opens, and Pexi's server asks RevenueCat whether Pexi Plus is active for your device identifier, so the weekly scan limit can be lifted. Tapping Restore Purchases contacts RevenueCat and Apple or Google.

Rough location, when your phone allows it. Pexi uses location only as far as your phone's own location permission for Pexi allows, which you set in the phone's prompt or its settings. Your phone works out your position and rounds it on the phone to a grid square about one kilometre wide. Only the grid square is sent. Pexi's server stores the grid square, not your exact position, and discards any exact coordinates a request might carry. Pexi uses the grid square to suggest nearby shops, and the shop you pick is stored with the scan.

Photos. The camera is used on your phone to read barcodes and text. This version of Pexi does not upload photos or camera images.

Pexi does not collect your name, email address, phone number, contacts, payment information, exact location or advertising identifiers.

Why Pexi uses it

  • To answer your scan and to look up nearby shops.
  • To work out whether a price is good, using prices Pexi holds, including prices that people have entered. Prices you enter can be used in answers shown to other shoppers.
  • To improve Pexi's own price data and answers, including by using collected scans to train and tune Pexi's own price estimates.
  • To find and fix problems, using the usage events, errors and server logs described above.

Who else receives data

Pexi's server sends limited information to these outside services to answer a scan. Open Food Facts, Anthropic and OpenStreetMap's Overpass service do not receive your device identifier. Cloudflare, which carries your requests, and RevenueCat, described below, do. The only one that receives anything about where you are is the shop-finding service, and only when your phone allows location.

  • Open Food Facts (world.openfoodfacts.org) receives a barcode number when Pexi's own catalogue does not know the product, to look up the product's name, brand and size.
  • Anthropic (the maker of the Claude AI model) receives a product's name, brand, size, category and country when Pexi has no price for it, as described under "AI price estimates".
  • OpenStreetMap's Overpass service receives the centre point of your rough grid square, only when your phone allows location, to find shops nearby.
  • Cloudflare carries traffic between the app and Pexi's server, so it handles your requests in transit, including the device identifier they carry. Cloudflare also stores an encrypted backup copy of the server, which it cannot read.
  • Apple provides the App Store, handles downloads, and processes Pexi Plus payments on iPhone. Pexi receives no card or Apple ID details from Apple.
  • Google provides Google Play, handles downloads, and processes Pexi Plus payments on Android. Pexi receives no card or Google account details from Google.

RevenueCat (revenuecat.com) is different from the list above: the app contacts it each time it opens, and Pexi's server contacts it to check whether Pexi Plus is active. It receives your random device identifier as the app user identifier, together with the purchase information from Apple or Google described under purchase history.

Pexi does not sell your data and does not share it with advertisers or data brokers.

Same protection from every service. Pexi shares user data only with the services named here, and each of them provides the same or equal protection of that data as this document states and as Apple's App Store Review Guidelines and Google Play's policies require.

Outside your province. Pexi's server and most of these services are outside Quebec, and some are outside Canada, including in the United States and the European Union, where privacy law differs. Pexi limits what each one receives to what is listed above.

How long Pexi keeps it

  • Server request logs: 90 days, then deleted.
  • Usage events: 12 months, then deleted.
  • Scans, ratings and prices you entered: after 24 months your device identifier is removed from them. What remains is a product, a price or an answer that is no longer tied to your phone, and Pexi keeps it to answer other shoppers.

Backups of the server can hold a copy for longer until they are replaced. You can ask for deletion sooner, as described below. Deleting the app does not delete what the server already holds, and on an iPhone the identifier stays in the Keychain, so a reinstall brings it back. On Android, a reinstall usually starts with a new identifier, and the records tied to the old one stay on the server until they are deleted on the schedule above. To have the records tied to your device deleted, use Delete my data in Settings.

Your rights, and how Pexi handles requests

  • You can ask to see, or delete, the records tied to your device. Open Settings and tap Delete my data, which prepares an email to usepexiapp@gmail.com that includes your device identifier so the right records can be found, or write to that address yourself. Deletion is done by hand.
  • If you think a price or verdict is wrong, you can say so in the app by answering the question about whether the verdict was right.

These are the steps Pexi follows, in plain words. Jamin Xu, named above, is responsible for them.

  • Requests to see or delete your data. Use Delete my data in Settings, or email the address above. Because Pexi holds no name or account, it finds your records by your device identifier, and it checks that the request comes from the person holding that phone before it shows or deletes anything. Pexi answers in writing within 30 days. A deletion removes the records tied to your device from Pexi's server, and the purchase record at RevenueCat if you subscribed. Server backups drop the copy within about 15 days. If you keep using the app on that phone, new records start again under the same identifier.
  • Complaints. Write to the address above. Pexi reads each complaint and answers in writing. You can also complain to the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (cai.gouv.qc.ca) or to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (priv.gc.ca).
  • Incidents. If personal information is ever lost, or seen or used by someone who should not have it, Pexi acts at once to stop it and writes the incident in a register, whether or not anyone was harmed. If an incident creates a risk of serious harm, Pexi tells the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec and the Privacy Commissioner of Canada promptly, and tells the people affected through a notice at the top of this document and in the app, because Pexi holds no email address or phone number for its users.

Prices and information you provide

If you type a price, choose a store, correct a verdict or rate an answer, you confirm that what you provide is true to the best of your knowledge. You allow Pexi to store it and to use it, together with other shoppers' contributions, to improve Pexi's price data and to answer other shoppers, as described in this document. To make that possible, you grant Pexi a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual and irrevocable licence to store, copy, adapt, combine with other data, publish and share what you provide, including under the open data licences described under "Data sources and licences". This licence covers the prices, store choices, corrections and ratings you submit, never your device identifier or location. Do not submit anything unlawful, misleading or that you have no right to share.

Pexi is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by any store, brand or data provider named in the app. Prices are what somebody recorded on the day shown beside them, not an offer, and not checked with the shop.

Acceptable use

  • Do not use Pexi for anything unlawful.
  • Do not try to break, overload, probe or reverse engineer Pexi or its server, or to reach another person's data.
  • Do not use scripts or automated tools to send requests to Pexi's server.
  • Do not submit false prices on purpose.

Pexi Plus subscription

Pexi is free to download. Pexi Plus is an optional auto-renewing subscription that gives 100 barcode scans a week, where the free allowance is 10 barcode scans a week. Typed searches are free and are not counted. When the weekly allowance is used, scans start coming back as the earliest ones pass seven days. It is sold through Apple's in-app purchase system on iPhone and Google Play Billing on Android, with purchases processed by Apple or Google and by RevenueCat.

  • Plans and prices. Pexi Plus Monthly is CA$3.99 a month. Pexi Plus Yearly is CA$29.99 a year. The price, in your currency, and the billing period are shown on the Pexi Plus screen in the app before you buy.
  • Payment. Payment is charged to your Apple ID account (iPhone) or Google Play account (Android) at confirmation of purchase.
  • Auto-renewal. The subscription renews automatically unless it is cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Your account is charged for renewal within 24 hours before the end of the current period, at the price of the plan you chose.
  • Managing and cancelling. You can manage and cancel your subscription in your Apple ID account settings on your iPhone (Settings, your name, Subscriptions), or on Android in the Google Play app (your profile picture, Payments and subscriptions, Subscriptions). Deleting the app does not cancel it.
  • Refunds. Refunds are handled by the store you bought from: Apple on iPhone, Google Play on Android.
  • Restoring. If you reinstall Pexi or use a new phone with the same Apple ID or Google account, open the Pexi Plus screen and tap Restore Purchases.

Security

The app talks to Pexi's server over an encrypted HTTPS connection. No system is perfectly secure, and Pexi cannot promise that data will never be accessed without permission.

No warranty

Pexi is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind, express or implied, to the extent the law allows. Pexi does not promise that the app or its server will be available at all times, uninterrupted or free of errors. The app depends on Pexi's server and may stop answering when the server is unavailable.

Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent the law where you live allows, Jamin Xu is not liable for any loss arising from your use of Pexi or your reliance on any price, verdict, estimate or other content shown by it, including a purchase made or not made because of it. Nothing in this document limits a liability that the law where you live does not allow to be limited. If you are a consumer in Quebec, this section does not apply to the extent it would free Pexi from the consequences of its own act or that of its representatives.

Changes and ending access

Pexi may change, suspend or stop at any time. We may update this document. If a change affects your Pexi Plus subscription, such as its price or what it includes, we will tell you in the app at least 30 days before it takes effect, and you can cancel before then at no cost. If you live in Quebec, a change applies to you only if it concerns your subscription's price, its allowance of scans or its features. You will get written notice at least 30 days before the change, showing the new clause and the old one, and you may cancel without cost or penalty up to 30 days after it takes effect. You can stop using Pexi at any time by deleting the app.

If Pexi changes what it collects or who receives it, this document will be updated and the effective date above will change. The version in the app and on Pexi's website is the current one.

Governing law

This document is governed by the laws of the Province of Ontario and the federal laws of Canada that apply there, without regard to conflict of laws rules. This choice of law does not take away the protection that the law of the place where you live gives you as a consumer.
